lessonRef.unitTitle: PF1 — Earning Income: Income, Benefits, and the Cost of Getting Qualified
lessonRef.title: Guided practice: cost and time of required education or technical skills

focus: cost and time of required education or technical skills
objective: Compute what a fictional technical certificate costs in money and time, and how long the resulting pay increase takes to repay that cost.
scenario: Lena Pham is a fictional worker considering an invented 18-month HVAC certificate program. The program, the tuition, and the wages below are all made up for this exercise.
safetyNotes: Every figure, person, employer, institution, offer, account, and document on this task sheet is fictional and exists only for practice.
No real transaction is part of this lesson, and no real bank, card, brokerage, tax, or login detail is ever requested. If a task sheet ever appears to ask for one, stop and tell a trusted adult.
This lesson teaches general financial concepts and does not advise anyone about their own money. For a real decision, talk with a trusted adult or a qualified licensed professional.
materials: the fictional program and wage figures in these directions

tasks.directions: The fictional certificate costs $6,800 in tuition plus $950 for tools and books, and takes 18 months. Lena currently earns $29,500 per year and expects $46,000 per year once certified.

prompts.text: What is the total out-of-pocket cost of getting qualified?
How much more would Lena earn per year after certifying?

tasks.directions: Payback time is the cost of qualifying divided by the yearly gain, expressed in months.

prompts.text: How many whole months of the higher wage does it take to repay the cost of qualifying? Round to the nearest month.
Counting the 18 months of the program itself, how long from starting the program until the cost is repaid?
Over 5 years at the higher wage, what is Lena’s net gain after subtracting the cost of qualifying?
If the program’s tuition rose to $19,000 with everything else unchanged, would the cost still be repaid within the first year of higher pay?
choices: No, it would take longer than a year

prompts.text: The payback calculation above leaves out something that costs Lena real money during the 18 months. Name it, and say how including it would change the answer to the payback question.

remediation: If payback is being computed as cost divided by the new salary rather than by the gain, put the two salaries side by side and ask which dollars are actually new. Only the $16,500 difference is available to repay the $7,750; the other $29,500 was already being earned.
extension: Suppose Lena must cut to half her current hours during the 18 months. Compute the earnings she gives up and redo the payback in months with that cost added.

evidencePurpose: Develop and apply education, career, cost, and uncertain outcomes through the existing fictional lesson work, including calculation where relevant and evidence-based decision reasoning.

conceptExplanation.title: Understand education, career, cost, and uncertain outcomes
paragraphs: Education and career choices combine direct cost, time, funding, work conditions, and uncertain earnings.

An estimate or average does not guarantee one person’s outcome. In this lesson, the learner uses the provided fictional facts about cost and time of required education or technical skills; no real household information belongs in the work.

A sound comparison uses the same time horizon and states assumptions and opportunity costs. The usable process is: Name the fictional goal and time horizon. Compare direct and recurring costs on the same basis. Include time, funding terms, and uncertain outcomes. Defend a conditional choice and test one changed assumption.
relationship: Name the fictional goal and time horizon.
Compare direct and recurring costs on the same basis.
Include time, funding terms, and uncertain outcomes.
Defend a conditional choice and test one changed assumption.
conceptExplanation.commonConfusion: The option with the highest stated earnings is not automatically best after cost, time, risk, and fit are considered.
conceptExplanation.conditionsAndLimits: Use only the stated fictional facts, time period, rate meaning, fees, taxes, timing, rounding, goals, and constraints. The result is education for this scenario, not individualized advice.

calculationPolicy.currency: USD where a prompt states USD
calculationPolicy.operationOrder: Use the learner-visible scenario order and apply only the stated inflows, outflows, rates, fees, taxes, interest, deposits, charges, or payments.
calculationPolicy.rounding: Treat exact-cent results as exact. When a prompt requires rounding, round only at its explicitly stated point and to its stated unit; use half-up for cent rounding unless the prompt declares another rule.
calculationPolicy.normalization: Follow each prompt’s requested unit and precision. Dollar and cent forms are equivalent only when the adult authority declares that normalization.
permittedTools: calculator when listed in lesson materials or task directions
calculationPolicy.verification: Protected fixed authority remains adult-only and is independently recomputed or comparison-derived from integer cents, basis points, exact rationals, or validated decimal strings. Binary floating-point output is never final authority.

workedExamplePolicy.separationRule: The model uses different fictional people, amounts, wording, and decision conditions from protected independent and mastery work.

workedExamples.title: Worked example — education, career, cost, and uncertain outcomes
workedExamples.fictionCue: Every person, amount, product, institution, and rule in this example is invented for instruction.
facts: Program A has an invented $1,200.00 cost and takes six months.
Program B costs $600.00 and takes three months.
Both meet the fictional job requirement; earnings after completion are unknown.
workedExamples.goal: Choose for a fictional learner whose constraint is completing within four months.
workedExamples.relevantInformation: Use only the listed fictional facts and conditions; do not substitute real household information.
workedExamples.method: Name the fictional goal and time horizon. Compare direct and recurring costs on the same basis. Include time, funding terms, and uncertain outcomes. Defend a conditional choice and test one changed assumption.
steps: State the decisive constraint: completion within four months.
Program A fails that constraint at six months; Program B meets it at three months.
Choose Program B under these facts, while noting that quality, funding terms, or verified outcomes could change the choice.
workedExamples.interpretation: The choice is conditional on the time constraint and equal qualification assumption.
workedExamples.reasonablenessCheck: Choose Program B under these facts, while noting that quality, funding terms, or verified outcomes could change the choice.
workedExamples.tradeoff: A longer program could be reasonable if it produced a verified benefit worth the extra time and cost.
workedExamples.limits: The conclusion applies only to the stated fictional facts. A changed rate, fee, time, rule, goal, constraint, or risk can change it.
workedExamples.calculationAuthority: All USD calculations shown here are written as integer cents. Percent rates, when used, are integer basis points divided by 10,000; stated rounding is half up at the declared line only.

guidedPracticeContract.learnerAction: Select and carry out the relevant operation with the fictional quantities, then interpret the result.
guidedPracticeContract.supportBeforeAction: Vocabulary, labelled facts, the approved separate model, and an empty organizer may be used only outside protected attempts.
guidedPracticeContract.feedbackAfterAction: Check for the observable confusion: The option with the highest stated earnings is not automatically best after cost, time, risk, and fit are considered.
guidedPracticeContract.expectedEvidence: A learner-produced calculation or comparison plus financial meaning in the learner’s own words.
guidedPracticeContract.fade: Step cues and parallel models end before independent or protected evidence.

independentScenarioContract.independentBoundary: Use only the stated fictional facts and declared tools. No completed step, selected option, decisive justification, or protected result may be supplied.
independentScenarioContract.responseForm: mixed exact calculation and written reasoning
independentScenarioContract.freshness: The protected case keeps the target but changes facts, constraints, timing, representation, or alternatives from the worked model.

decisionReasoning.gradeBandDemand: Test assumptions, compare interacting constraints, defend a conditional decision, and identify residual risk.
framework: Identify fixed facts, constraints, and assumptions.
Compare relevant benefits, costs, risks, and opportunity costs.
Use a calculation only when it answers a decision question.
Defend a conditional choice and name a changed fact that could change it.
decisionReasoning.neutrality: More than one conclusion may be defensible when priorities differ; scoring follows relevant evidence and internal consistency, not an adult lifestyle preference.

masteryRule.independenceRule: Worked examples, completed organizers, answer-bearing hints, or decisive feedback invalidate the protected attempt; use a fresh case after support.
masteryRule.evidenceRequired: Correct or acceptably normalized fixed work plus aligned financial interpretation or decision reasoning.
masteryRule.decisionRule: Mastery is decided only by the aligned adult-only authority for the named evidence lesson; completion alone is not mastery.

remediationRoutes.observableSignal: The option with the highest stated earnings is not automatically best after cost, time, risk, and fit are considered.
remediationRoutes.alternateExplanation: Use a labelled fact–rule–result–meaning organizer. Separate what the fictional case states from what must be calculated or judged, then connect the result back to the stated goal.

parallelWorkedCase.title: Alternate model — education, career, cost, and uncertain outcomes
parallelWorkedCase.fictionCue: This is a different invented case, not a protected task answer.
facts: Two fictional courses both qualify a learner; one costs 45,000 cents and takes eight weeks, the other costs 30,000 cents and takes twelve weeks.
parallelWorkedCase.representation: Write each money amount as integer cents, label the goal and constraints, and keep assumptions beside the calculation or comparison.
steps: Choose based on the stated fictional priority rather than price alone.
Name a changed funding or schedule fact that could reverse the choice.
parallelWorkedCase.check: Reverse the arithmetic where possible and confirm that the conclusion uses a stated goal or constraint.

remediationRoutes.guidedRetryRule: Use the alternate representation on a different fictional case, require the learner to complete the decisive step, and fade labels after the attempt.
remediationRoutes.freshMasteryRule: Use a fresh protected case after support; do not count the parallel model or supported retry as mastery.

hintPolicy.mustNotReveal: Protected results, winning options, decisive justifications, adult authority, or enough successive steps to reduce the response to copying.
hintPolicy.independenceEffect: A parallel worked case or answer-bearing help ends the current independent attempt and requires fresh evidence.

agePolicy.reasoningDemand: Test assumptions, compare interacting constraints, defend a conditional decision, and identify residual risk.

answerPolicy.workedExampleSeparation: Learner-visible examples are separate instruction and never authority for protected task responses.
